denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 81455 (targeted genomic sequence analysis panel, solid organ neoplasm, 51 or more genes) with date of service 2026-01-25. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. Payer remark: Multi-gene panel testing is considered investigational for this diagnosis based on the documentation submitted.

criteria.text: Recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III or IV cancer.
The patient is seeking further cancer treatment and the result will inform the selection of therapy.
The same tumor panel has not previously been performed for this primary cancer.

The panel is an FDA-approved or cleared companion diagnostic, or its use is recommended by National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines for the tumor type (RAS, BRAF, HER2, microsatellite instability, and NTRK status for metastatic colorectal cancer).

chart.text: Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.9, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Sigmoid colon biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Mismatch repair proteins intact by immunohistochemistry.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
CT chest, abdomen, pelvis with contrast: circumferential sigmoid mass with regional nodes, 3 hepatic lesions in the right lobe, largest 3.6 centimeters, consistent with metastases. No lung lesions.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 16 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

51 year old woman in medical oncology after colonoscopy for a change in bowel habits found a sigmoid mass. Long conversation about what stage IV means and what treatment looks like. She is realistic and motivated. ECOG 1. Port referral placed. Her history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, seasonal allergies. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works from home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Stage IV sigmoid adenocarcinoma with synchronous liver metastases. She wants treatment. Results will determine whether she is a candidate for anti-EGFR antibody therapy, BRAF-directed therapy, HER2-directed therapy, or immunotherapy, and the chemotherapy backbone will start while we wait. No prior molecular testing on this tumor; the biopsy block is available at pathology. Ordering the solid tumor next-generation sequencing panel to cover KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, HER2 amplification, microsatellite status, and NTRK fusions in one assay, per NCCN for metastatic colorectal cancer.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Back to start treatment. Panel sent to the reference laboratory today from the biopsy block. FOLFOX cycle 1 scheduled for next week; we will adjust the biologic once the molecular results are back. Vitals today 114 over 89, pulse 67.
A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 56 denial can be answered from the record.
